payload.title: The anchor and split arbiters are minted at the later cycle's workspace HEAD instead of the sha the pair judged, so whenever main moved the closing set spans two shas, consensus refuses it as target_sha_mixed and the paid third answer never becomes an anchor
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cycle.py:2014 (target_sha is the workspace HEAD resolved for this cycle)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/cycle.py:2214-2219 (the anchor arm mints the arbiter with that HEAD)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1195-1222 (the arbiter is minted with the passed target_sha; a group already minted for these inputs is skipped as already_dispatched)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judge_fanout.py:1135-1136 (a group that already holds ANCHOR_MIN_JUDGE_COUNT judge rows, the arbiter's included, is no longer an anchor candidate)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/judgment_bridge.py:570 (the ai_judge row's target_sha is the request's mint sha)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/feedback_store.py:1521-1532 (an anchor-grade closing set with more than one target_sha is refused as target_sha_mixed)
aria-kernel/tests/test_jj1_anchor_consensus.py:583-588 (the test builds the two-sha case and pins the refusal; nothing pins that the arbiter is minted at the pair's sha)
payload.rule_violated: ARIA-HIGH-004 and J5: a closing set is judged at one tree; the producer must mint the third seat at the tree the pair judged (feedback_store.py:1513-1520 names the arbiter answering after the tree moved as the realistic path).
payload.notes: The pair settles at sha A in cycle N; the arbiter is minted in a later cycle at that cycle's HEAD B. Main advanced 8 to 14 first-parent commits per day over 2026-10-21..27 (git log --first-parent at d716541239), so A and B differ. The arbiter answers at B, generate_ai_consensus sees two shas, records target_sha_mixed and writes no anchor row, and because the group now holds three judge rows and its arbiter inputs are already minted, nothing re-asks it. The only input the acceptance bar accepts is starved, plan_synthesizer.scan_f_findings is fed almost no promoted true positives, and every arbiter answer is paid for and discarded. Close condition: Carry the pair's common target_sha on the group (derived from its ai_judge rows with _common_target_sha) and mint the arbiter at it; when the seats themselves span two shas mint nothing and write a named hold. Test: a pair at sha A plus an arbiter minted while HEAD is B yields an anchor-grade row and no target_sha_mixed uncertainty (red today); keep MixedTargetShaAnchorTests for the consensus-side refusal. Plan row: F0.7 and the J-series follow-up (not scheduled). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
